speaker: Asa
text: There's good dirt under all this moss. Who's been using it?

speaker: Asa
text: I can't go on... come back for me.

speaker: Asa
text: You're not from the village. Doesn't matter. Help me with this sack.

speaker: Bjarne
text: Anything else?

speaker: Bjarne
text: Where's the anvil? No, don't tell me. I'll find it.

speaker: Bjarne
text: Tell Sigrid I kept it lit.

speaker: Bjarne
text: You took your time. Mind the hammer.

speaker: Bjarne
text: I blazed the trees going in, a cut every twenty paces. Coming back, my marks were on the wrong side of them. The road hadn't moved. The roots had moved it, under us, in the night. Tor was thrown further in than me, with a bad leg. Listen for a saw where nobody saws.

speaker: Eirik

speaker: Eirik

speaker: Eirik
text: Weapons up!

speaker: Eirik
text: Clear. Get your breath.

speaker: Eirik
text: That's the last of them.

speaker: Eirik
text: I trust that she wants to get out of here alive. That is enough for tonight. But watch her hands when she talks about the stones. She knows more than she says.

speaker: Eirik
text: My sister's farm is two valleys from here. Her dogs ran into these woods last month and never came back. Someone has to walk in front. Better me than you.

speaker: Eirik
text: Once, as a boy, with my sister. Spruce, moss, the quiet you get in old woods. Nothing in it frightened me but the dark. I would like that to still be true.

speaker: Eirik
text: Twenty winters in the shield wall at Granheim. I stopped counting the fights a long time ago. I still count the friends.

speaker: Eirik
text: Wolves, probably. Perhaps a witch, perhaps a sick troll. It is usually less than the stories and more than you packed for. Four friends, if we are lucky. Bjarne owes me money.

speaker: Eirik
text: Eat something, even if you are not hungry. I have buried enough friends who thought they could fight on an empty stomach.

speaker: Eirik
text: Stay between me and the trees. If anything comes out of the dark, it meets my shield first.

speaker: Eirik
text: Hold still. Drink this.

speaker: Eirik
text: Not yet, you don't. Drink.

speaker: Eirik
text: You're bleeding. Here.

speaker: Eirik
text: Eat something. It is a long road, and the porridge is not getting any better.

speaker: Eirik
text: Go! I will hold them. Nobody gets left behind, not while I am standing.

speaker: Eirik
text: Anything else?

speaker: Eirik
text: Come back when it's done.

speaker: Eirik
text: Before we set out? Gladly. Take this practice sword; it bruises, it doesn't cut. Hit the dummy by the fire until your arm knows the way, then come and try it on me.

speaker: Eirik
text: Dry bread, unless you fancy a walk. There are berry bushes in the clearing west of the shelter. Pick five and stew them over the fire; take my waterskin for the pot. Be quick about it. I do not like how quiet it is.

speaker: Eirik
text: Now that is a fine idea. Anything but this porridge. Here is a rod and a handful of grubs, and the lake is just south of the road. Two fish, and I'll owe you.

speaker: Eirik
text: We always need firewood. Take this hatchet; there are good trees on the slope north of the road. Six logs will do us.

speaker: Eirik
text: Breakfast! You may be the best person on this expedition. Keep the rod; there is bound to be water in those woods.

speaker: Eirik
text: Hot food. You have just made three friends for life. Take these, in case the night is not done with us.

speaker: Eirik
text: That will keep us warm. Keep the hatchet.

speaker: Eirik
text: You'll do. Better than most I have trained, worse than you will be. Take these; you will want them.

speaker: Eirik
text: Dummy first, then me. Watch my shoulders: the blow is coming when they drop.

speaker: Eirik
text: Five berries from the clearing to the west, then the pot. My waterskin is in your pack.

speaker: Eirik
text: Six logs from the slope north of the road. Walk up to a tree and get chopping.

speaker: Eirik
text: Two fish from the lake. Hold attack to swing back, let go to cast, and strike when the float goes under.

speaker: Eirik
text: Show me the wall. Then show me where it's weakest.

speaker: Eirik
text: Behind you, you fool!

speaker: Eirik
text: Go. I've held worse.

speaker: Eirik
text: Still got one more swing in me, then.

speaker: Eirik
text: Ugh. Took your time.

speaker: Eirik
text: Twenty winters, and it still hurts.

speaker: Eirik
text: Don't look at me like that. I was resting. ...Thank you.

speaker: Eirik
text: My knees are too old to run from a closing portal. Next time leave earlier.

speaker: Eirik
text: That many, and I'm still here. Don't tell the young ones. They'll want to try it.

speaker: Eirik
text: Twenty winters I've been telling that kind of story. First time it's been true.

speaker: Eirik
text: Took you long enough. How many are behind you?

speaker: Eirik
text: Finally, something I can hit.

speaker: Eirik
text: Stay behind my shield, if you can find it.

speaker: Eirik
text: Clean your blade. It's a bad habit to forget.

speaker: Eirik
text: Is that all? I was only warming up.

speaker: Eirik
text: A soldier's choice. It is old iron, but it holds an edge. Guard well and let them come to you.

speaker: Eirik
text: Eirik. Twenty winters in the shield wall at Granheim. I walk in front, I carry the heavy things and I make sure everyone eats. There is porridge. It is bad.

speaker: Eirik
text: Long reach, and it wants both hands. If you ever need a light instead, press L to swap them.

speaker: Eirik
text: The axe. Good. It splits wolves and firewood alike, and it leaves you a hand free.

speaker: Eirik
text: Then we are after the same thing. We will find them.

speaker: Eirik
text: A bewitched forest. My grandmother called any forest that ate her goats bewitched.

speaker: Eirik
text: A whole day gone in a morning's walk. I don't like this, and I have liked very few things.

speaker: Eirik
text: And the kindling you cut this morning is dry in your pack. We only need stones.

speaker: Eirik
text: And there is only dry bread, unless someone fancies a walk. Ask me if you do.

speaker: Eirik
text: Down you go. Catch your breath; we go again when you're ready.

speaker: Eirik
text: Enough, enough! I yield. You'll do.

speaker: Eirik
text: Good. Now me. When I wind up, raise your guard just before the blow, or roll through it.

speaker: Eirik
text: I salted what was left of your fish, so we need fewer berries. Two handfuls will do.

speaker: Eirik
text: Is it past noon already? We have not been walking an hour.

speaker: Eirik
text: It is this place. At the tree line I had to think for my own sister's name. I did not like to say.

speaker: Eirik
text: Nothing gets worse than this porridge.

speaker: Eirik
text: Sigrid. The sun is going down. It was morning.

speaker: Eirik
text: Steady now. It is a fine morning to walk into something stupid.

speaker: Eirik
text: That trout this morning. I keep thinking about that trout.

speaker: Eirik
text: Twenty years a soldier, and I have never seen the sun simply leave.

speaker: Eirik
text: Whoever you came for: we have not stopped looking. Remember that.

speaker: Gunnar
text: You've been frightening my deer. Least you can do is give me a roof.

speaker: Gunnar
text: I can't go on... come back for me.

speaker: Gunnar
text: Took you long enough. That boar's been lying on me since yesterday.

speaker: Hild
text: Whoever laid this hearth had never met a level. I'll stay.

speaker: Hild
text: I can't go on... come back for me.

speaker: Hild
text: Mind the coping. It's the only level thing for a mile.

speaker: Ingrid

speaker: Ingrid
text: The plants are wrong. Roots that should sleep in this season are warm to the touch. Something is feeding the enchantment. Stay close; I brought a little medicine.

speaker: Ingrid
text: We came to learn why this forest has become bewitched. First, we need shelter. Follow the old road.

speaker: Ingrid
text: Hold still. Drink this.

speaker: Ingrid
text: Not yet, you don't. Drink.

speaker: Ingrid
text: You're bleeding. Here.

speaker: Ingrid
text: Stay near the stones. We can still get out of this together.

speaker: Ingrid
text: Anything else?

speaker: Ingrid
text: I kept saying the word so the forest couldn't take it. Fire. Fire. Fire. And then I saw yours.

speaker: Ingrid
text: I can't... go on. I'll hide here. Come back for me.

speaker: Ingrid
text: It's you! I saw a light through the trees and thought the forest had finally taken my wits. Get me out of here.

speaker: Ingrid
text: I watched your fire for three nights from under a root. You should know two things. The old troll at the stones didn't come for us: it came for the door. And on the second night something walked past my root in Granheim mail, like Eirik's. I called to it. It turned, and it didn't know its name. When the stones broke I heard Bjarne's hammer start up, somewhere deep in the woods, slow, like he's working one-handed. Let me be of use until we find them.

speaker: Liv

speaker: Liv

speaker: Liv

speaker: Liv
text: That's the last of them.

speaker: Liv
text: There are old paths here, older than the villages. My teacher said the waystones connected places of shelter. I thought that was only a story.

speaker: Liv
text: We came to learn why this forest has become bewitched. First, we need shelter. Follow the old road.

speaker: Liv
text: Hold still. Drink this.

speaker: Liv
text: Not yet, you don't. Drink.

speaker: Liv
text: You're bleeding. Here.

speaker: Liv
text: The stones are answering you. Stay close. I will try to keep the passage open.

speaker: Liv
text: Anything else?

speaker: Liv
text: Your ward is a promise too. Did anyone tell you?

speaker: Liv
text: Write it down. Somebody has to write it down.

speaker: Liv
text: The stones broke along a line. A line! Do you understand what that means?

speaker: Notice Board
text: Come back when it's done.

speaker: Notice Board
text: "To whoever comes after: this hearth wants copper, and hands that can work it. Smelt ingots and make a pickaxe. What I left behind this board is yours." - the last smith

speaker: Runa
text: Behind you! Turn!

speaker: Runa
text: On your back!

speaker: Runa
text: I owe you one.

speaker: Runa
text: Still here. Still here.

speaker: Runa
text: Thank you. I thought that was it.

speaker: Runa
text: I'm bleeding!

speaker: Runa
text: They're too close, I need room!

speaker: Runa
text: I'll hold this spot.

speaker: Runa
text: I'll keep back.

speaker: Runa
text: Nothing gets to you without going through me.

speaker: Runa
text: Point the way.

speaker: Runa
text: Right behind you.

speaker: Runa
text: Contact! I've got the range.

speaker: Runa
text: Moving, there!

speaker: Runa
text: All clear.

speaker: Runa
text: Nothing else moving.

speaker: Runa
text: Deer, boar, wolf, all running west out of the trees, out here where they don't belong. Nothing sleeps in the open unless it is afraid to sleep at home.

speaker: Runa
text: Poaching on the jarl's land. You learn to hit with the first arrow when the second one brings the wardens.

speaker: Runa
text: Someone is paying. And I would rather know what is coming out of there than wait for it to find me.

speaker: Runa
text: Troll tracks. Small ones, the moss kind. They never come this far down. Something is pushing everything out of the high woods, and it is big.

speaker: Runa
text: Walk where the moss is thick; it's quieter. Keep your back to the fire, never your face. And if you hear something heavy breathing, don't run until I say so.

speaker: Runa
text: I counted three wolves circling and one shape that was not a wolf. Keep your voice down. I would rather see them before they see us.

speaker: Runa
text: Tracks everywhere, all running the same way. Whatever they are fleeing, we are walking towards it. Lovely.

speaker: Runa
text: Hold still. Drink this.

speaker: Runa
text: Not yet, you don't. Drink.

speaker: Runa
text: You're bleeding. Here.

speaker: Runa
text: Nice morning. That is usually how it starts.

speaker: Runa
text: I will take the ones on the stones. You just keep breathing.

speaker: Runa
text: Anything else?

speaker: Runa
text: Wolves! They are not hunting; something is driving them towards us. Protect the camp!

speaker: Runa
text: More of them, coming round the other side!

speaker: Runa
text: Come back when it's done.

speaker: Runa
text: As it happens. There are blight boar on the grass north of the road, east of the camp, which is wrong all by itself, and we could use the meat. Take my spare bow: hold the left button to draw, let go to shoot. Bring down two.

speaker: Runa
text: Clean enough. Keep the bow; you've earned it, and I was tired of carrying it.

speaker: Runa
text: Two boar, on the grass north of the road, east of the camp. Hold the left button to draw.

speaker: Runa
text: This place can be found. Good. So can everything else, by the same road.

speaker: Runa
text: Behind you! Turn around!

speaker: Runa
text: I know the way. Go on. I'll catch you up.

speaker: Runa
text: Bow's still good. So am I.

speaker: Runa
text: Move. I've got your back.

speaker: Runa
text: Too close, too close!

speaker: Runa
text: I counted our steps to the exit. I'd rather not count that close again.

speaker: Runa
text: I've tracked things my whole life, and never one that big. It left nothing behind but quiet. I don't trust the quiet.

speaker: Runa
text: The forest doesn't hate us. It doesn't notice us. That's worse. Next time I pick the way.

speaker: Runa
text: You crossed open ground to reach me. Stupid. Don't stop.

speaker: Runa
text: I've watched you for two days. You leave a trail like a cart.

speaker: Runa
text: I see them. Take the near ones.

speaker: Runa
text: There! In the trees!

speaker: Runa
text: Nothing else on the wind.

speaker: Runa
text: That's all of them. I think.

speaker: Runa
text: A bow! Then there are two of us. Hold the left button to draw, let go to shoot. It wants both hands: if you ever need a light instead, press L to swap them.

speaker: Runa
text: An honest answer. I like you already.

speaker: Runa
text: Down! Moss trolls in the bushes, the small kind. Don't let them get behind you!

speaker: Runa
text: It followed us! The old one, coming through the trees, right for the stones!

speaker: Runa
text: It hasn't seen us yet. It will smell the smoke soon enough.

speaker: Runa
text: Liv.

speaker: Runa
text: Off the road, on your left! Rootlings. They were lying in wait, and they don't do that.

speaker: Runa
text: Runa. I find the tracks, and I shoot what makes them. Trolls off their crags, witches on the roads, wolves that don't run from fire. I want to see it for myself before I believe any of it.

speaker: Runa
text: Simple. I respect that. Hit it until it stops, and it leaves you a hand free.

speaker: Runa
text: Small ones never come alone and never come this far down. Something up in the high woods is scaring them. Finish the berries and get back to the fire.

speaker: Runa
text: A shepherd told me his dogs won't go past the tree line any more. Dogs. I have seen those dogs go after a bear.

speaker: Runa
text: Boar, running flat out, and not from us. Off the road!

speaker: Runa
text: Hold up. That's Bjarne's handcart, tipped off the road. Have a look; I'll watch the trees.

speaker: Runa
text: No birds. Have you noticed? Not one for a while now.

speaker: Runa
text: Sigrid. Look behind us. Where is the road? It was right there, and now there's only mist.

speaker: Runa
text: Still think the coin is worth it?

speaker: Runa
text: The shadows are wrong. They were behind us when we crossed the stream.

speaker: Runa
text: There. Feel that? The wind turned, and there is mist coming up off the moss.

speaker: Runa
text: Wolves behind them! In the open, in daylight. They don't do that. Weapons!

speaker: Runa
text: You shot straight this morning. It may matter before the night is out.

speaker: Runa
text: Your grandmother never saw wolves walk into a lit camp.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Behind you!

speaker: Sigrid
text: Watch your back!

speaker: Sigrid
text: I owe you one.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Still here. Still here.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Thank you. I thought that was it.

speaker: Sigrid
text: I can't take much more of this.

speaker: Sigrid
text: I'm hurt!

speaker: Sigrid
text: I'll hold this spot.

speaker: Sigrid
text: I'll keep back.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Nothing gets to you without going through me.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Point the way.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Right behind you.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Here they come!

speaker: Sigrid
text: Weapons up!

speaker: Sigrid
text: Clear. Get your breath.

speaker: Sigrid
text: That's the last of them.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Because the only old things out there are stones and roots, and the marks on them are older than any village. Whatever is wrong, I expect to find it written down.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Eirik sees a great deal for a man who pretends not to. Yes. I have seen stones like these before, and I know what they do. Ask me again when you have to touch one.

speaker: Sigrid
text: I know what it feels like: a door left open in winter. Someone opened it on purpose. Whether they meant to let something in or out... that is what we came to find.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Ingrid, Bjarne, Tor and Liv. An alchemist, a smith, a carpenter and a scholar: the ones who can make sense of what they find. I sent them on two days ago to look over the old road. It was a short job.

speaker: Sigrid
text: The cause. Trolls do not leave their crags for no reason, and wolves do not forget fire. Something in that forest has changed, and the villages want it named before it reaches their doors.

speaker: Sigrid
text: They did not send me. They asked for someone who could read the old marks, and I was the only one who answered. Draw your own conclusions. Everyone else does.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Words for things your tongue has no names for. Most of them mean wait. One of them means open. Pray we only need the first kind.

speaker: Sigrid
text: The villages think we came for wolves and witches. Let them. The stones out here are older than any village, and someone has been waking them.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Keep the torch high and the road under your feet. The forest is listening tonight. Let it hear only footsteps.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Hold still. Drink this.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Not yet, you don't. Drink.

speaker: Sigrid
text: You're bleeding. Here.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Take what time you need, but not too much. It is a long walk, and I want to be at the forest by noon.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Stand inside the ring. Whatever you see, do not let go of the stone until I say.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Anything else?

speaker: Sigrid
text: Dry stone overhead. Good work. Now a fire, before anyone can think clearly: eight sticks and twelve small rocks off the forest floor, then build it beside the shelter (G).

speaker: Sigrid
text: That was no weather. The sun went down hours early and this storm came out of a clear sky. Ingrid, Bjarne, Tor and Liv walked into this two days ago, so we go on, not back. Follow the old road into the trees and find us dry shelter. We are right behind you.

speaker: Sigrid
text: The packs are tied and the fire is nearly out. Ingrid's party should have been back yesterday, and the forest is half a morning down the road. If you have anything left to do here, do it now: once we set out, we do not come back for it. Are you ready?

speaker: Sigrid
text: The stones are drawing power! Hold them off until the connection forms!

speaker: Sigrid
text: There you are. Come and stand by the fire with the rest of us. You should know who you are walking with before we set out.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Come back when it's done.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Hold together! Nobody gets left behind. We will find each other, whatever happens.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Finish your porridge and listen. This is the only quiet you will get today.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Stay on the road. We keep a steady pace, and the others will wait if you fall behind.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Seven went in. Tell me who's home.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Behind you! Move!

speaker: Sigrid
text: Don't you stop for me. That's an order.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Back in line. Thank you.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Good. On your feet. I mean, on mine.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Still standing. Barely.

speaker: Sigrid
text: A retreat is only a defeat if you learn nothing. What did we learn?

speaker: Sigrid
text: I gave you an order once to leave me if it came to that. You didn't. We'll talk about discipline. Later.

speaker: Sigrid
text: I've buried good people on less than what we just did. Write it down somewhere. It should outlast us.

speaker: Sigrid
text: I've served under worse than you. Don't let it go to your head.

speaker: Sigrid
text: You came back. I told them you would.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Form up on me!

speaker: Sigrid
text: Stand together! Nobody runs!

speaker: Sigrid
text: Count heads. Everyone still here?

speaker: Sigrid
text: Good. Move before more come.

speaker: Sigrid
text: ...can anyone hear... Ingrid was right behind me when the stones broke. She's hurt. Find her first. Do you hear me? Find her first...

speaker: Sigrid
text: A fire. Sit down, all of you, and get your breath back. Whatever is out there will still be there when we are done.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Almost! Hold it off, just a little longer!

speaker: Sigrid
text: At first light we find the four who went ahead. Ingrid. Bjarne. Tor. And...

speaker: Sigrid
text: Careful. The ones who go looking for the truth of it are the ones who find it.

speaker: Sigrid
text: For anyone who slept through last night's talk, and I know who you are: I am Sigrid, and we walk east today. The villages asked what is wrong in that forest. Two days ago I sent Ingrid, Bjarne, Tor and Liv ahead to look. They should have been back yesterday.

speaker: Sigrid
text: It will not wake for me. It never has. You, then. Put your hand on the centre stone.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Leave the fire! Take the old path north, to the standing stones. Now!

speaker: Sigrid
text: Liv. Of course. Eleven years I have known her, and for a moment there was a hole where her name should be.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Roots do not set ambushes on a road. Something taught them to. Keep moving. We need walls around us before more of them wake.

speaker: Sigrid
text: That is no thunder. An old one, a mountain troll, and it is walking towards our fire.

speaker: Sigrid
text: We leave when you are ready. If you want to earn your porridge first, ask the others. They always have something.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Whatever you see, do not let go of the stone. There are things I should have told you, and there is no time left to tell them.

speaker: Sigrid
text: You asked me by the fire, so here it is. I have seen stones like these wake once. It took everyone who stood too near, and it put them somewhere else. Ingrid knew that when she came. Now you do.

speaker: Sigrid
text: I can see that. Light your torches, and take this one.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Keep walking.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Not alone, and not before we are ready. Come back to the others.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Rumours grow in the telling. That is why we go and look, instead of sitting in a longhouse and listening.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Save it for the road. We have until the porridge gets worse.

speaker: Sigrid
text: Wolves that hunt by day and do not fear four armed people. Whatever happened to this cart was quick, and it did not end here. We go on.

speaker: Sigrid
text: You wanted to know if the stories were true. How are you finding it?

speaker: Sigrid
text: And you. You came to us with a strong back and few questions. Nobody walks towards that forest by accident. Why are you here?

speaker: Sigrid
text: Then one thing first. Nobody walks that road unarmed. We carry spare arms in the packs. They are old and they are plain, but they will do. Take what suits you.

speaker: The Portal
text: A fire first, little one. Fallen branches and loose stones lie all around me: pick them up, open the build menu (G) and light it inside my ward. The sooner it burns, the sooner they can see it.

speaker: The Portal
text: A horn at dusk, the expedition's signal. She is the last of them. Bring her home, little one.

speaker: The Portal
text: A saw, out where nobody saws. Your carpenter is hurt, but he is still measuring.

speaker: The Portal
text: A snare line, a mile of it, and at the end a man who did not mean to be caught.

speaker: The Portal
text: A wall went up overnight out there, round nothing. Whoever built it will want to build a better one here.

speaker: The Portal
text: Bare hands bring little home, little one. A hatchet in your belt and a pick beside it bring wood and ore. Sticks and sharp stones: make them in your bag (B).

speaker: The Portal
text: Come and sit by me, little one. There is something I should have told you before you went to that hollow.

speaker: The Portal
text: Go, little one. She is just beyond me, off the path. Come back through one of my doors before I close. What you wear I can always bring home. What you carry I cannot.

speaker: The Portal
text: Listen, little one. Rest your hand on the stone.

speaker: The Portal
text: Listen. A hammer, far off in the deep woods, slow and uneven. One of yours. Ask me what the woods hold before you go, and I will tell you where.

speaker: The Portal
text: Marks on the trees that only the dark shows. Go through at night.

speaker: The Portal
text: My ward keeps out the worst of the forest, not all of it. Put a wall between your fire and the trees.

speaker: The Portal
text: Now bring me what you freed. Feed me that light and I will open for you, as I did in the dark.

speaker: The Portal
text: Now feed yourself. Berries, water from the stream, a stew over your fire. You will be walking people home.

speaker: The Portal
text: Now the woods have told me. Something breathes under the roots, little one, in a hollow deep in the Misty Woods: a guardian, as old as my stones. It will not wake for steel. Take an ember from your own fire to it. That, it cannot ignore.

speaker: The Portal
text: Old stones are humming in the deep woods. Someone is inside the ring, writing.

speaker: The Portal
text: One fire brought Ingrid home. The others will want more than a fire: a bench, a furnace, a dry place to set down what they carry. Build what they will need.

speaker: The Portal
text: One weapon is one answer, and it will not last for ever. Make a second at your workshop: a club stuns what a blade only cuts.

speaker: The Portal
text: She is close, little one. Just beyond me, off the path, hiding. Find her, keep her near you, and bring her through.

speaker: The Portal
text: Smoke from a farmstead that burned long ago. Someone kept the seed.

speaker: The Portal
text: Someone is cooking out there. The wolves can smell it. So can I.

speaker: The Portal
text: Something tests my ward. Out there, someone else is holding a clearing against the wolves. Bring him to hold mine.

speaker: The Portal
text: The brighter this place burns, the further it can be seen. Build. Clear the old growth. Give them something worth walking towards.

speaker: The Portal
text: The forest has put its roots in even here. Three stones around the clearing still hold my light, choked and cold. Free them, and bring the Life Orbs back.

speaker: The Portal
text: The light that reached her reached other things as well. They are on the old path now, testing me. Prepare yourself. When you are ready, tell me, and I will let them come.

speaker: The Portal
text: What you carry through me, the woods can take from you. What you leave here, I keep. Build a chest beside your workshop (G), and put in it what you cannot bear to lose.

speaker: The Portal
text: You brought the woods home on your back. Now make something of them: a lodge by the trees, a saw that turns logs into planks. The smithy and the walls start with a plank.

speaker: The Portal
text: You have a fire. Now a roof to work under: a workshop beside it (G). What the woods break, it mends.

speaker: The Portal
text: A hundred winters I kept this clearing alone. I had forgotten how loud a home is. Do not stop.

speaker: The Portal
text: Every hearth in my light is a little more of the old pact kept.

speaker: The Portal
text: I listen for your people every night. Some nights I hear them.

speaker: The Portal
text: The forest cannot forget a place that someone tends.

speaker: The Portal
text: A fire first. Then a home worth coming back to. Then we go and fetch them. And one day, little one, you will tell me why these old stones woke for your hand.

speaker: The Portal
text: Did you see what grew out of them as they fell? Root. The same root that choked my stones, and closed the road behind your people.

speaker: The Portal
text: Do you feel that? The ward has remembered what it is for. And far out in the mist, little one, someone has stopped walking and turned to look.

speaker: The Portal
text: I am a door, little one, and I have gone to sleep. I am too thin to wake myself. Long ago people kept a hearth beside these stones, and I kept the night from their door. That was the pact. No fire has burned here in a hundred winters.

speaker: The Portal
text: I have not told you everything. The Heartroot was no monster. It was the forest's guardian: its half of the pact. Your kind let the hearth beside me go cold a hundred winters ago. It kept its half for ninety winters after that, alone, until the hunger got into its roots.

speaker: The Portal
text: It is all one thing, little one. Something old is pushing those roots, from somewhere deep in the woods. When the woods tell me where, I will tell you.

speaker: The Portal
text: Its last word was for you. Hearth-keeper. Nobody has called anyone that in a hundred winters, and I did not teach it to you. One day you will tell me why these stones woke for your hand.

speaker: The Portal
text: Listen. Far off, at dusk, a horn: three long notes and a rest, over and over. The expedition's signal. Someone out there has seen your light and is answering it.

speaker: The Portal
text: Look, now that there is light to see by. Three of my stones, choked in roots. And the roots are moving, little one. Slowly. Towards me.

speaker: The Portal
text: My stones have gone quiet, but she is right. One spark burns close, just beyond me, hiding from the wolves. Make yourself tools, and go.

speaker: The Portal
text: Seven sparks, scattered through the Misty Woods. They are alive. I hear them when the wind is right. But the forest does not kill the lost, little one. It forgets them.

speaker: The Portal
text: So light one. The forest cannot forget a hearth that someone tends. It will feed my ward, and out in the mist your people will see it and know which way is home.

speaker: The Portal
text: The last of an old promise. I keep the dark from this clearing. But that is not what you need to know.

speaker: The Portal
text: Then she is still herself, and she is holding on. She will want the others home before her. Bring them, little one, and keep this fire high.

speaker: The Portal
text: There. A hearth beside my stones, after a hundred winters.

speaker: The Portal
text: With its roots gone quiet I can reach further. North, past the troll country, the road is open. The old one that broke my stones the night you fell walks that road. It came for the door then. Go carefully.

speaker: The Portal
text: With what? You have nothing but your hands, and I cannot open.

speaker: The Portal
text: Would you have woken it, knowing? It could not be saved, only stopped. Better by the hand of someone who keeps a hearth.

speaker: The Portal
text: You brought it down. Lay what you carried out of the hollow by the fire, little one, where it can feel the warmth. It is owed that much.

speaker: The Portal
text: You came for coin. There is none here. Stay anyway. They need you to.

speaker: The Portal
text: You came for coin. There is none in this. But there is a debt now, and you have begun to pay it.

speaker: The Portal
text: You came for someone. Every one of your people is out there because of what was let go cold. Bring them home, and the debt grows smaller.

speaker: The Portal
text: You came looking for someone. Now there are others looking for you. Let them find a light.

speaker: The Portal
text: You came to see if the stories were true. Here is the one nobody tells: we broke the pact first.

speaker: The Portal
text: You came to see whether the stories were true. Now you are one of them.

speaker: The Portal
text: Your people did, long before you were born. You are mending it. Every fire kept here is a payment on that debt.

speaker: The Portal
text: And the guardian under the roots, who kept the forest's half. Where is it now?

speaker: The Portal
text: And this. Their door, and the night kept from it, for as long as the fire burned.

speaker: The Portal
text: I remember this. A fire beside my stones, and someone to keep it.

speaker: The Portal
text: Little one, behind you! My ward is too thin yet. They are coming up through it.

speaker: The Portal
text: Rootlings, in my clearing. Feed me those orbs, and they will not get in so easily again.

speaker: The Portal
text: First the way home. Then their names. Then there is no one left to find.

speaker: The Portal
text: That is what you killed. I am sorry. Someone had to.

speaker: The Portal
text: Warmth stirs in the old stone. Little one. You fell out of the dark with the whole forest at your heels, and I caught you. I could only catch one.

speaker: Tor
text: Behind you!

speaker: Tor
text: Watch your back!

speaker: Tor
text: I owe you one.

speaker: Tor
text: Still here. Still here.

speaker: Tor
text: Thank you. I thought that was it.

speaker: Tor
text: I can't take much more of this.

speaker: Tor
text: I'm hurt!

speaker: Tor
text: I'll hold this spot.

speaker: Tor
text: I'll keep back.

speaker: Tor
text: Nothing gets to you without going through me.

speaker: Tor
text: Point the way.

speaker: Tor
text: Right behind you.

speaker: Tor
text: Here they come!

speaker: Tor
text: Weapons up!

speaker: Tor
text: Clear. Get your breath.

speaker: Tor
text: That's the last of them.

speaker: Tor
text: This stone is dry enough. Give me sound timber and a little daylight, and I could make somewhere worth staying. For now, this fire will do.

speaker: Tor
text: We came to learn why this forest has become bewitched. First, we need shelter. Follow the old road.

speaker: Tor
text: Hold still. Drink this.

speaker: Tor
text: Not yet, you don't. Drink.

speaker: Tor
text: You're bleeding. Here.

speaker: Tor
text: Stay near the stones. We can still get out of this together.

speaker: Tor
text: Anything else?

speaker: Tor
text: It's built crooked, you know. All of it. Give me a week.

speaker: Tor
text: My tools. Leave them, if you have to. Not me.

speaker: Tor
text: Still measuring. I knew someone would come, and I wanted something to show for it.

speaker: Tor
text: There's a hollow in the deep woods where nothing grows, and the ground breathes there. In, out, slow as a sleeper. I lay three nights on this leg listening to it. Whatever is down there is old, and it's what moves the roots. Now, where do you want your planks?

speaker: Yrsa
text: Show me your kitchen. No, on second thought, show me what you eat.

speaker: Yrsa
text: I can't go on... come back for me.

speaker: Yrsa
text: Mind the pot. If you've come to eat, you'll carry.
